# Corpus files on which the simple reader reads right: the right columns and the right number of rows.
# HAND-LABELLED: each file was checked by reading its cells, not by comparing the two readers. The layout reader
# must read every file listed here exactly as the simple reader does (tests/test_corpus.py). Add a file only after
# checking the simple reading by hand; corpus.py --refresh never changes this list.
#
# Not listed, on purpose:
#   r3-transposed_kv.csv: both readers take the first record (Name, Alice) as the header; neither is right.
#   r1-all_text_survey_long_headers.csv: the simple reader is right, and the layout reader shortens the long question names on
#     purpose (the full text is kept as each column's header).
#   r1-single_row.csv, r1-title_only.xlsx: the simple reader drops the only row; the layout reader keeps it as data.
#   r7-side_by_side_same_rows.csv: two blocks with the same header row and rows are read as one table on purpose
#     (a blank spacer column inside one table looks the same); both readers give one table.
#   every other file: the simple reader misreads it (sections, notes, units rows, stacked or side-by-side tables, merged titles,
#     page-break repeats, preambles without a full row, a numbers-only table).
